records.text: The Flying Machine is a vehicle found in Sholazar Basin.

The Avatar of Freya identifies as the Lifewarden, an embodiment of one aspect of Freya left to defend Sholazar from the Scourge. Holding back undead armies leaves living cultists to be confronted by allies, whose worth can exceed initial expectations. Protective duty outweighs reluctance to unleash the destructive Etymidian. The Avatar also seeks to conserve the fallen Lifeblood Pillar's energy for healing the land.

Hemet Nesingwary hunts Sholazar's largest game, testing newcomers against rhinos and laughing off druids trying to stop him. Farunn's horn only whets his appetite for larger, fiercer prey. He also cares about the camp's people, recalling worry when Helice failed to return from a crystal-hunting trip. He recommends The Green Hills of Stranglethorn to those interested in joining his safaris.

Monte Muzzleshot was meant to bring supplies to Hemet's Sholazar expedition but is stranded and begs to be cut down. He warns newcomers that the jungle is dangerous, especially with the Venture Company around, and disparages the archmage who sent them. He directs travelers to Hemet's camp and asks that someone there be sent to help him.

Dreadsabers are unusually formidable Sholazar Basin cats: Hemet's account says they can bring down larger game than he has seen other cats hunt. They range in the wilderness around the Nesingwary camp and south of the river, where hunters are challenged to prove themselves against them.

Mangal crocolisks are described as wily river and mangal predators, found along the southern river and in Wildgrowth Mangal to the east. The expedition's hunting trial uses them as a test of a hunter's skill.

Bittertide hydras inhabit Bittertide Lake in Sholazar. Their caustic sputum is valuable for Archmage Pentarus' studies, and they spray it when engaged; Colvin Norrington seeks samples for that research.
Goretalon rocs are wild creatures found in Sholazar. They use a swooping attack when fighting.
Shardhorn rhinos are powerful, large game that rule the wilds northwest of Hemet's camp. The expedition's rhino trial challenges hunters to face them, and they charge when engaged.
Stranded threshers are found in two Sholazar Basin areas.
Emperor Cobras threaten the Rainspeakers’ hatchlings. In combat, an Emperor Cobra can spit poison.
A Rainspeaker Warrior serves as a fighter among the Rainspeakers.
A Rainspeaker Oracle holds an oracle role among the Rainspeakers.

High-Oracle Soo-say is a Rainspeaker who describes their home as sacred and seeks help protecting its hatchlings from Emperor Cobras. Soo-say asks an adventurer to offer peace to Shaman Vekjik, saying the Rainspeakers want to avoid a fight, and sends help to Mistwhisper Refuge with a warning to strike back if attacked. Soo-say also watches the adventurer closely and says they trust them to carry out the peace mission.

Buck Cantwell is a hunter with Hemet Nesingwary’s expedition at the Nesingwary Base Camp. While injuries keep him from ranging into the basin, he tests hunters’ skill as trackers and follows Debaar’s report of Shango’s tracks. Though initially unsure the great dreadsaber exists, Buck accepts the evidence and praises a successful hunt.

Debaar works with Hemet Nesingwary’s hunting expedition at its base camp, scouting the basin and preparing camouflage for dangerous hunts. She regards the Venture Company’s attacks on the expedition’s scouts and supply flights as an insult, yet says a game hunter cannot rightly raise a weapon against another person. She also shares responsibility for the expedition’s plans against dangerous game.

Weslex Quickwrench is the mechanic responsible for the Spirit of Gnomeregan, the expedition's flying machine, damaged when the ship ran aground. He asks for an engine and spare parts, then patches her up with whatever is available. He calls her a poor flying machine and warns riders about saw blades in the seat; he hopes to restore her proper form in Dalaran.
The Spirit of Gnomeregan is a flight master. When attacked, it can summon an Enraged Gryphon and an Enraged Wyvern.

Purser Boulian is an innkeeper who sells goods and offers lodging. In one remark, he says this is not quite what he signed up for, though at least it is warm; the line gives him a wry note of resignation about his present circumstances.
Mardan Thunderhoof is a gunsmith who sells goods and ammunition and repairs equipment. His listed services cover both restocking and weapon upkeep.

Korg the Cleaver cooks for the hunters at Nesingwary's camp, favoring tender longneck grazer meat over the tough, stringy fare hunters bring back. After the shipwreck, he is glad they can leave salt beef behind and toast their comrades with a proper meal.

Hadrius Harlowe is the camp's stablemaster and one of Grimbooze Thunderbrew's trusted taste-testers. He says he is always up for Grimbooze's drinks, jokes that the Jungle Punch tastes like something his wife would drink, then approves of its familiar kick.

Lucky Wilhelm is the living target in Drostan's rifle lesson, with an apple set on his head. Grazed shots draw complaints about his ear and mustache, and he threatens to quit the target business; a good shot earns a quick compliment.
A Frenzyheart Berserker is a combatant whose defining response to serious wounds is a sudden frenzy: badly hurt, it erupts into rage.

A Frenzyheart Tracker follows the tribe's enemies. When angered, it calls the listener a “big-tongue lover,” declares them no longer a friend of the Frenzyheart, and threatens that the Frenzyheart will get them.

A Frenzyheart wolvar fighter in the conflict around Sparktouched Haven and the nearby shrines. Oracles describe the wolvar as attacking their settlements and damaging sacred places; this ravager is among the nearby wolvar they ask the player to fight. Its recorded combat behavior includes a frenzy and Whirlwind.

A Frenzyheart wolvar hunter found with its people in the Sholazar Basin conflict zone. Its recorded combat action is to shoot; the supplied evidence gives it no individual dialogue, service, or story role.

A Frenzyheart wolvar spearbearer in the camp conflict north of Mistwhisper Refuge. Mistcaller Soo-gan asks the player to stop the Frenzyheart from disturbing the sacred Great Stones, and identifies spearbearers among those to kill. This fighter uses Skewer in combat.

A Frenzyheart wolvar scavenger in the camp conflict north of Mistwhisper Refuge. Mistcaller Soo-gan asks the player to stop the Frenzyheart from disturbing the sacred Great Stones, and identifies scavengers among those to kill. This fighter throws a spear in combat.

High-Shaman Rakjak is a Frenzyheart wolvar who trains outsiders as hunters and sends them to gather resources before entrusting them with larger work. He treats recruits as slaves and laughs at the killing of rival apes, speaking with blunt confidence in his role.
Serfex the Reaver is a named hostile creature in Sholazar Basin. When combat begins, Serfex is held in place.
Sapphire Hive Drones are common hive insects found across several parts of Sholazar Basin. Frenzyheart hunting instructions include killing them during an apprentice's wasp hunt.
Sapphire Hive Wasps are hive insects found across several parts of Sholazar Basin. A Frenzyheart apprentice is sent to hunt them as part of learning the hunt.
The Sapphire Hive Queen is a hostile hive creature that becomes enraged in combat.
Sholazar Tickbirds are birds found across several parts of Sholazar Basin.

Tracker Gekgek is a Frenzyheart hunter who fiercely claims his kills and treats the player as a new slave after one is taken. He taunts with his spear and sends the supposed slave to High-Shaman Rakjak, while directing a hunt and demanding that prey be brought back intact.
Hardknuckle Chargers are creatures hunted alongside Hardknuckle Foragers under Goregek's direction.

Pitch is a singular lion regarded as a formidable hunting trophy. Tamara Wobblesprocket describes him as a ferocious beast and says rumors place his home near the Wildgrowth Mangal and Skyreach Pillar; she wants his remains as proof of a notable hunt.
Hardknuckle Foragers are creatures hunted alongside Hardknuckle Chargers under Goregek's direction.

Blighted Corpses are hostile undead among the forces threatening the Lost Lands. Freya calls for their destruction alongside Bonescythe Ravagers as she focuses on the danger posed by the Lich King's forces.

Urgreth of the Thousand Tombs is a Scourge commander in Sholazar Basin. He declares the land belongs to the Lich King, rallies his followers to crush opposition, and insists that nothing can stop the Scourge.

Shaman Jakjek is a Frenzyheart shaman who praises a fighter's skill with traps and says only the strongest Frenzyheart learn the secret Vekgar taught. His replies call battle fun and encourage the fighter to return for more, showing an enthusiastic focus on combat and tribal strength.

Lightningcaller Soo-met is a Sparktouched oracle who speaks in clipped Common. He worries that the puppy-men have attacked for days, though he says the Great Lightning Stone remains safe. Soo-met expects Soo-holu to help the Oracles, drawing on the protector’s power against the attackers.
Bonescythe Ravagers are beasts among the Scourge forces threatening the Lost Lands. Freya’s quest identifies them as targets to destroy, and they attack with a bone-saw ability.

Mistwhisper Warriors are combatants found around the Mistwhisper area. Their combat behavior includes casting a spell; Zepik’s account identifies Mistwhisper Gorlocs as the group involved in disrupting the rain shrine.
Mistwhisper Oracles are combatants found in the Mistwhisper area. Their behavior includes casting a spell when engaged.
A Sparktouched gorloc warrior in Sholazar Basin, one of the nearby big-tongues targeted in Kartak’s ritual hunt. In combat, it uses Lightning Whirl.
A Sparktouched gorloc oracle of Sholazar Basin. In combat, it casts Forked Lightning, distinguishing its lightning magic from the warrior’s Lightning Whirl.

A severely injured Mosswalker who speaks for its people in the aftermath of an attack. It wonders why they were harmed despite giving shinies to the shrine, offers its shinies, and asks for better weather and the undead to go away. When helped, it thanks the “dryskin.”

Mistcaller Soo-gan tends the Great Mist Stone at Mistwhisper Refuge and resents the Frenzyheart “puppy-men” for damaging its sacred shrines and taking treasure. Soo-gan asks for help stopping the intruders and recovering the treasure, then directs a successful helper back to Soo-say at Rainspeaker Canopy. Soo-gan jokes about being short and admits the stone is cared for “most of the time.”

Lafoo is an eager digger who likes bugs and shiny things. Lafoo says High-Oracle Soo-say sent them to accompany you, and hopes to find offerings for the shrine by digging around the village. Their cheerful talk turns to concern when their bugs go missing.

Moodle is a wary, outspoken Mosswalker who fears for their people and doubts that the undead will leave peacefully. After the Lifeblood Pillar fell, Moodle connected the changed weather and undead threat to the damaged pillars, and hopes crystals may help protect the Mosswalkers. Moodle argues that the dead deserve respect and that any survivors should be rescued, while insisting the undead leader must be stopped. Though Moodle can sound condescending, they say they never want one of their people to die.

A Venture Company excavator working among the company's crews at Swindlegrin's Dig. The company has obstructed the Nesingwary expedition, antagonizing its scouts and shooting down supply flights, putting this worker on the hostile side of the camp's dispute.
Venture Company ruffians belong to the workforce accused of harassing Nesingwary's scouts and shooting down supply flights. Their combat repertoire includes Backhand and Bonk.
Softknuckles are beasts that Goregek proposes tormenting with a poker to lure the Hardknuckle Matriarch from hiding.
Longneck grazers are grazing beasts whose combat attacks include Hoof Strike.

Elder Harkek is a Frenzyheart elder and hunter who helps High-Shaman Rakjak with hunting tasks and handles requests involving the tribe’s hunters. He worries about food and values smart, capable people. When the player is suspected of treachery, he says he is glad Zepik proved them trustworthy and that they make him proud.
A young Frenzyheart pup who eagerly wants to see what is happening. The pups also warn others to run when they hear that Metalhead ate Rejek.
A young gorloc hatchling found among the gorlocs of Sholazar Basin.
An escaped Frenzyheart chicken that can be captured for Elder Harkek. It casts Frenzyheart Chicken: Invisibility.
A Frosthowl screecher, an aggressive creature that attacks with Shadow Bolt. It is found in multiple parts of Northrend, including the Borean Tundra and Sholazar Basin.

Foreman Swindlegrin is an antagonist tied to the Venture Company operation at Swindlegrin’s Dig. The local account identifies Meatpie as his bodyguard and says they probably occupy a platform overlooking the operation.
Meatpie is an ogre bodyguard to Foreman Swindlegrin at Swindlegrin’s Dig. The account of the operation describes him as large and mean, and warns that he may keep visitors from reaching the foreman.

Oracle Soo-rahm is a local oracle near the Bones of Nozronn. Soo-rahm asks for emperor cobra fangs as an offering toward an oracle’s necklace and prepares incense so Nozronn can answer a visitor’s question. Soo-rahm speaks as “we” and trusts Nozronn to know what the visitor seeks.
Cerberon is an undead in Sholazar Basin.
Hailscorn is a dragonkin enemy listed among the threats Etymidian is sent to slay at the Avalanche. In combat, it casts Ice Claw, Wing Buffet and Skeleton Army.
Glonn is an undead creature found in Sholazar Basin.
Bythius the Flesh-Shaper is a formidable undead who uses Poison Spray in combat. The Avatar of Freya names him among the threats for Etymidian to destroy in Sholazar Basin.

The Hardknuckle Matriarch is fiercely protective of her young, screaming with rage and rushing to their aid. Goregek's plan is to draw her out by provoking the Softknuckles, making her the target of his hunt.

Goregek the Gorilla Hunter is a quest-giving hunter who treats the player as a servant, ordering them to bring food while he rests or hunts. He boasts of wanting the Hardknuckle Matriarch and plans to draw her out by provoking Softknuckles. His blunt, self-important speech makes his domineering attitude clear.

Zepik is an adventurous Gorloc hunter who has traveled widely and enjoys stories about beasts, dragons, and gods. He learned hunting from Dajik but says he does better his own way; Elder Harkek helped him when he was young and disliked Dajik. Zepik relishes hunting the Mistwhisper Gorlocs and can show exuberant, theatrical excitement.

An injured Rainspeaker Oracle, this Gorloc rises clumsily and speaks for a group returning home. The oracle says home is nearby and urges its companion to come along, giving the rescue a practical role as a guide back toward the village.

A Snowblind Ghoul is an undead creature found in the Avalanche and another part of Sholazar Basin. It is included in the Reclamation objective to deploy Etymidian and slay Scourge forces and named enemies.
A frostbitten undead corpse found in Howling Fjord.
A particularly formidable risen undead in Howling Fjord, this reaver stands out among the dead as an elite fighter.

Professor Calvert works with Wes on restoring a flying machine. Concerned by unusual weather approaching from the northeast, he has a pilot ready and directs a prospective copilot to Pilot Vic at Lakeside Landing.
An arranged crystal formation in the Mistwhisper area.
Farunn is described as a powerful rhino and the target of Hemet Nesingwary's hunt in Sholazar Basin. Hemet's account calls the beast exceptionally strong and says its horn commemorates the kill.
Shango is a dreadsaber of the Sholazar Basin, known in local stories for his exceptional size and ferocity. Buck Cantwell sends trackers to identify his tracks and seek his pelt.
A captive crocolisk responds to an approaching visitor with a low growl.

Shaman Vekjik is a hostile Frenzyheart shaman who warns that visitors are unwelcome in Frenzyheart land and threatens to use magic against the big-tongues. When approached with a peace offering from them, he says he does not want to be bothered.
A Servant of Freya is an elemental identified as serving Freya.

Drostan tests marksmanship at Nesingwary Base Camp, lending an RJR Rifle to shoot an apple from Lucky Wilhelm’s head and warning against careless aiming. Competitive and confident, he challenges a hunter to count kills while helping Hemet’s expedition and stresses endurance over speed. He brushes off complaints about the shooting mishaps. When beaten, his reward response admits he underestimated the challenger and honors a fair victory.
Crunchy is Debaar’s pet.

Venomtip is a particularly large snake threatening the hatchlings near Rainspeaker Canopy’s waterfall. High-Oracle Soo-say identifies it as one of the snakes the locals want stopped; Venomtip fights with Cobra Strike and spits poison.

A Cultist Infiltrator is a living servant of the Lich King and a Cult of the Damned trespasser in Freya’s basin. The Lifewarden describes the cultists as a threat to the land and directs the player against those at Death’s Hand Encampment; this infiltrator is armed with a Ticking Bomb.

Zootfizzle works at Dorian’s Outpost, where Dorian has him training and feeding captured baby drakes. He is doing research of his own and wants a pet roc, weary of robotic pets whose joints need oiling. He also makes a point of keeping the outpost free of cogs and mocks people who use them.

Dorian Drakestalker is a hunter at his outpost, familiar with Hemet Nesingwary and working alongside Zootfizzle. He sees the local drakes as ideal quarry and plans to draw Broodmother Slivina into a hunt, with hatchlings gathered for Zootfizzle. Away from the hunt, he is content tending the fire and talking with Zootfizzle about cogs, and jokes that Weslex’s cogs are another way to spend time at camp.

Primordial drakes are dangerous wild creatures of the area north and east of Dorian’s Outpost. Dorian describes them as capable of devouring a person and uses a hunt against the lesser drakes to prepare for the larger challenge of Broodmother Slivina; one drake ability is called Birthing Flame.
Shattertusk Mammoths are large local mammals found around the Savage Thicket.
Shattertusk Bulls are male members of the local mammoth population. They are encountered around the Savage Thicket and can use a trampling attack when fighting.
A Shattertusk Calf is a young member of the local mammoth population found in the Savage Thicket.
A primordial hatchling in the Sholazar Basin caves can be picked up, after which it disappears. Its name and pickup behavior identify it as a young creature rather than a speaking character.
A primordial drake egg found in the Sholazar Basin caves.
Thalgran Blightbringer is a Scourge monster whom Freya's Avatar blames for corrupting the land. He casts Birth out of combat and uses Deathbolt and Rain of Fire in combat.

This burned Cult of the Damned corpse is a grim clue to the cult’s presence in Sholazar Basin. Though dead, it remains a quest contact: reports about the Scourge’s living agents and the Lifeblood Pillar’s destruction are tied to it.
Fruit Tosser, a Sholazar Basin figure.
Broodmother Slivina is a fierce, protective mother whose young have been taken. A hunt for revenge brings her into conflict with those who stole them.

Chad is a deckhand who signed on for Nesingwary’s expedition after learning Miss Boulian would be there. He had planned to propose to her, but the shipwreck separated him from his engagement ring; he believes it is somewhere in the Basin.
Wants Banana is a demon in Sholazar Basin.
A Cult of the Damned saboteur, this hostile combatant attacks with thrown dynamite.

“Tipsy” McManus is Grimbooze Thunderbrew’s assistant and works with a fruit distillation. He directs the addition of oranges, papayas, and bananas, monitors pressure, and tells the operator when to open the valve. His remarks show practical familiarity with the still and its changing needs.

Tamara Wobblesprocket is Marvin’s wife, sent with him at Hemet’s request to help establish the Lakeside Landing camp and repair flying machines. She wants to improve her hunting skills and hopes to make a respected trophy of the lion Pitch. She also samples Grimbooze’s Jungle Punch and bluntly compares its taste to engine degreaser.

Marvin Wobblesprocket is Tamara’s husband and a flight master at Lakeside Landing. Hemet says he asked the couple to establish a camp and use their flying machines to relay supplies and survey the area. Marvin offers fast travel and works at the camp with Tamara.
Blighted Corpses are undead creatures found across several parts of the area.

Artruis the Heartless is a long-warring undead who boasts that he cannot die and taunts challengers as mortal. He admits that the surrounding crystals weaken him, a vulnerability he underestimated. He recognizes the conflict between two rivals and offers the player a choice of sides, while invoking Arthas as a possible path to power.

If the player saves the Oracles, Jaloot welcomes them as a friend and thanks them. Wary of the undead after being caught with his back turned, he vows to fight back. He says he will meet the player at Rainspeaker Canopy after retrieving a shiny object from the lich.

If the player saves him, Zepik the Gorloc Hunter recalls hunting alongside them and thanks them. Though he says he is no great admirer of the big-tongues, he feels they deserved a fair fight. He offers to tell the Frenzyheart that the player is no traitor and argues for restoring their friendship.

Pilot Vic is a flying-machine pilot and cold-weather flying trainer who recruits a co-pilot to investigate strange weather for the professor. He calls the route uncharted and admits he would not risk it alone. Afterward he thanks his companion for saving his life. He also loses his machine's keys, offers a nearly empty air tank for the search, and cautiously identifies a giant woman fighting Scourge as a possible lifewarden described by the professor.

Colvin Norrington gathers animal reagents at Dorian's Outpost for Archmage Pentarus's research in Dalaran. He asks for help collecting roc talons and hydra samples, presents the work as service to Dalaran's cause, and hints that local rumors may hold something worth investigating. He relays a gorloc saying about talons without claiming it as fact. His reward banter is wry: after the hydra samples, he advises a hot bath if the collector's burning sensation continues, and mentions what he endured to honor Hemet's bargain.

At Swindlegrin’s Dig, Engineer Helice is an explorer who came to sample the pillar’s crystals before Venture Company forces overpowered and detained her. During her escape, she warns the goons about explosives and meets the danger with sardonic jokes, even inviting them to help dispose of their own explosive cargo.
Explosion Guy.
A Storm Revenant is an elemental fighter that calls lightning in battle.
An aqueous elemental spirit attacks with Typhoon when fighting.
A giant metal Stormwatcher is a target of Rejek’s plan to make a helmet from its head. He suggests Venture Company explosives near Suntouched Pillar as a way to remove it.

Oracle Soo-nee teaches songs connected with the storms and waters of Sholazar. Her brief replies thank visitors for their help, and she says that learning her way can make them smarter or happier. She offers to teach a good song when the conditions for that conversation are met.
Perch Guardian is a guardian creature found around Maker's Perch. It casts Rune Punch in combat.
Grakjek is a fletcher who offers goods to browse. His local role is that of a bowyer's supply vendor.
Shaman Partak serves as a supplier of reagents and poisons. Visitors can browse his goods.
Wild Growth Stalkers are small creatures found in the Sholazar Basin area.
Loomee is a collector of shinies who offers goods to browse. Her local role is that of a vendor with ammunition and repair services.
A Servant of Freya is an elemental identified as serving Freya.
Soo-jam sells reagents and poisons.

Rejek proudly calls himself the Frenzyheart tribe’s youngest warrior and hopes to become mighty. His father gave him a sword, and he asks an older warrior’s help to blood it on the tribe’s foes according to tradition. Rejek seeks strength from heartblood, skyfire and seized elemental power, mocking the “big-tongues” for singing to clouds. Eager to frighten enemies, he shows off his new helmet and anticipates fighting alongside a helpful outsider.
A Goretalon Matriarch is a beast identified as a matriarch among the Goretalons.

The Shrine of the Tempest stands on the western side of Stormwright's Shelf. Rejek directs adventurers carrying the essences of wind and water there in pursuit of the tempest's power. The shrine manifests that power in a lightning strike against nearby targets.
Soo-yum is a food-and-drink vendor in the Rainspeaker Canopy area, offering goods to visitors who browse the stall.
Rarkag runs a food-and-drink stall in the Northrend settlement where he is based. Customers can browse his goods, making him a local vendor serving travelers and residents.
The Monstrous Wight is an undead creature whose combat behavior includes casting Smash.
The Lifeblood Elemental is an elemental creature whose combat behavior includes casting Blood Tap.
Scrapper Zartson is a humanoid in Sholazar Basin.
Rakat is a humanoid in Sholazar Basin.
Ajark is a humanoid in Sholazar Basin.
Vekgar is a Frenzyheart ally fighting the Sparktouched Gorlocs at Kartak's Hold. He shares a Frenzyheart strength secret with a new ally and urges them to help drive the attackers away.

Oracle Soo-dow is among the Oracles defending Sparktouched Haven from Frenzyheart wolvar attacks. He treats the player as a trusted friend and seeks help protecting his people, drawing on sacred crystals and the Great Ones' lingering protection.

Grimbooze Thunderbrew is a brewer whose expedition's shipwreck cost him his best kegs, leaving the jungle camp short of drink. Resourceful and hands-on, he turns gathered fruit into a new punch while leaving the still's operation to his assistant. He treats the tasting as a social debut, asking trusted friends for opinions and joking about the result.

Elder Sandrene frames the new-year moon observance as a time when the ancients awaken and welcomes homage to the olden races. Her public role connects her with fellow elders: visitors may ask her where Wanikaya, Bluewolf, or Arp is.

Elder Wanikaya reflects on an earlier hunting way of life, recalling pursuit for glory and honor and wondering whether the present is truly different. Her words give her a contemplative, tradition-minded outlook. Visitors may ask her where Sandrene, Bluewolf, Arp, or Pamuya is, linking her publicly with the other elders.
A Nesingwary Game Warden assigned to the local zone.
Geen is the Oracles Quartermaster. Customers can browse goods through Geen's vendor service.
Tanak is the Frenzyheart Quartermaster. Customers can browse goods through Tanak's vendor service.
Aotona is a named creature that fights with Eye Peck and Wing Buffet.
King Krush is a named beast with Charge and Mortal Wound in its combat repertoire.
Loque'nahak is identified as the mate of Har'koa. In combat, it uses Pounce and Frozen Bite.

An Alliance Flame Warden tending the Sholazar Basin festival fire. The Warden welcomes visitors honoring the flame and urges them to honor Alliance fires and desecrate Horde fires, reflecting the festival's factional rivalry.

A Horde Flame Keeper tending the Sholazar Basin festival fire. The Keeper welcomes visitors honoring the flame and urges them to honor Horde fires and desecrate Alliance fires, reflecting the festival's factional rivalry.

place_records.text: You are in Sholazar Basin, a Northrend land held by neither the Alliance nor the Horde. It is jungle and lake country, with Nesingwary Base Camp and Lakeside Landing as its main settlements. Frenzyheart wolvar and Sparktouched gorlocs contest the land around their shrines. Dreadsabers, hive wasps, rhinos and crocolisks roam the wilds.

You are in The Avalanche, an area of Sholazar Basin. Frostbitten corpses and snowblind ghouls are the commonest dangers, with frost screechers and risen reavers also here. Cerberon and Hailscorn are among the notable creatures.

You are in The Lost Lands, a part of Sholazar Basin where the Mosswalkers have been attacked. An injured Mosswalker asks for the undead to go away and for better weather. Blighted corpses, monstrous wights and bonescythe ravagers prowl here, and a servant of Freya is among the elementals.

You are in Nesingwary Base Camp, a hunting camp in Sholazar Basin run by Hemet Nesingwary's expedition, with an inn, a flight master and a stable master. Hemet Nesingwary hunts the basin's largest game, and Weslex Quickwrench is restoring the Spirit of Gnomeregan, the expedition's flying machine, after the ship ran aground.
You are in The Seabreach Flow, a stretch of Sholazar Basin where Mangal crocolisks and emperor cobras are the chief dangers. A Nesingwary game warden is assigned to the area.

You are in Kartak's Hold, a part of Sholazar Basin where Frenzyheart wolvar and Sparktouched gorlocs are at war. Frenzyheart ravagers and hunters attack the gorlocs here, and Shaman Jakjek is among the Frenzyheart. Sparktouched warriors and oracles fight back.

You are in Sparktouched Haven, a haven of Sparktouched gorlocs in Sholazar Basin, under attack from Frenzyheart wolvar. Lightningcaller Soo-met, a Sparktouched oracle, says the wolvar have attacked for days but the Great Lightning Stone remains safe. Dreadsabers are a danger here too.
You are in The Path of the Lifewarden, a route in Sholazar Basin where Frenzyheart ravagers and hunters are found alongside Sparktouched warriors. Longneck grazers graze among them.

You are in River's Heart, a spot near the centre of Sholazar Basin where the rivers converge. A spirit healer is here, and stranded threshers are the danger. Evil spirits are said to plague the waters, according to the Rainspeakers.

You are in Rainspeaker Canopy, the sacred village of the Rainspeakers in Sholazar Basin. High-Oracle Soo-say seeks help protecting the village's hatchlings from emperor cobras. Oracle Soo-nee teaches songs of storm and water. The village has a smith and merchants selling food, reagents and goods.

You are in Frenzyheart Hill, the camp of the Frenzyheart wolvar in Sholazar Basin. High-Shaman Rakjak trains outsiders as hunters and treats them as slaves. Elder Harkek worries about food for the tribe and values capable people. The camp has a smith and stalls.

You are in Wildgrowth Mangal, a jungle stretch of Sholazar Basin where emperor cobras and mangal crocolisks are the chief dangers. Monte Muzzleshot, a stranded supply man, warns that the jungle is dangerous with the Venture Company about. Shaman Vekjik, a hostile Frenzyheart shaman, is also here.

You are in The Sundered Shard, a part of Sholazar Basin where lifeblood elementals and bonescythe ravagers attack. Blighted corpses are here too, and Artruis the Heartless is among the dangers. An injured Mosswalker speaks for its people after an attack.

You are in The Lifeblood Pillar, a site in Sholazar Basin where the Lifeblood Pillar has been brought down. A burned Cult of the Damned corpse still marks the cult's presence there, and bonescythe ravagers and a monstrous wight haunt the ground around it.

You are in Mosswalker Village, a Mosswalker settlement in Sholazar Basin that was attacked. A severely injured Mosswalker speaks for its people, wondering why they were harmed after giving shinies to the shrine. Bonescythe ravagers and blighted corpses still roam the village.

You are in Hardknuckle Clearing, a clearing in Sholazar Basin where hardknuckle chargers and a hardknuckle matriarch make the ground dangerous. Sapphire hive wasps fly here too. Softknuckle beasts live in the clearing, and Goregek wants to torment them to draw the matriarch out of hiding.
You are in Sapphire Hive, a hive in Sholazar Basin where sapphire hive drones and wasps are the main dangers.

You are in Mistwhisper Refuge, a refuge in Sholazar Basin where Mistcaller Soo-gan tends the Great Mist Stone. Soo-gan resents the Frenzyheart for damaging the sacred shrines and taking the refuge's treasure.
You are in The Glimmering Pillar, a pillar in Sholazar Basin. A Servant of Freya, an elemental that serves Freya, is found here, and cultist saboteurs are the main danger.

You are in Spearborn Encampment, a camp in the conflict north of Mistwhisper Refuge. Frenzyheart wolvar spearbearers and scavengers fight here, and Mistcaller Soo-gan wants them stopped from disturbing the sacred Great Stones.
You are in The Bonefields, a stretch of Sholazar Basin where goretalon rocs feed on corpses. A goretalon matriarch and Shattertusk bulls are among the dangers here.

You are in Dorian's Outpost, a camp in Sholazar Basin where the hunter Dorian Drakestalker works. His companion Zootfizzle trains and feeds captured baby drakes. Colvin Norrington gathers animal parts here for Archmage Pentarus's research in Dalaran.

You are in The Savage Thicket, a thicket in Sholazar Basin where primordial drakes and their eggs are the main dangers. Primordial hatchlings are found in the caves, and Shattertusk mammoths are found around the thicket.

You are in Lakeside Landing, a camp in Sholazar Basin that Marvin and Tamara Wobblesprocket set up to repair flying machines and carry supplies. Marvin is the flight master here, and Pilot Vic, a cold-weather flying trainer, is also here. A strange weather pattern comes from the northeast, and the professor wants it investigated.
You are in Bittertide Lake, a lake in Sholazar Basin where bittertide hydras are the main danger. Mistwhisper warriors are found here as well.

You are in Rainspeaker Rapids, a neutral stretch of Sholazar Basin in Northrend. The Avatar of Freya, who calls itself the Lifewarden, keeps watch over the land against the Scourge, and Servants of Freya, elementals serving her, are about. Scourge undead have pushed into the basin, and Bonescythe Ravagers and Frosthowl Screechers haunt the rapids.

You are in Frenzyheart River, a neutral waterway in Sholazar Basin. An injured Rainspeaker Oracle, a gorloc, waits on its banks for a rescuer to lead it home to the village nearby. Hardknuckle Foragers hunt here under Goregek's direction. Blighted Corpses and Bonescythe Ravagers roam the river, and Stranded Threshers are found in its waters too.

You are in Wintergrasp River, a neutral river in Sholazar Basin, watched over by Servants of Freya, elementals serving her. Sapphire Hive Wasps and Drones swarm its banks, and Serfex the Reaver roams here. Mangal Crocolisks and Emperor Cobras lurk in the water and grass.

You are in Swindlegrin's Dig, a neutral site in Sholazar Basin. Venture Company goblins hold the pillar here under Foreman Swindlegrin, with excavators and ruffians about. Engineer Helice, an explorer who came for the pillar's crystals, was detained here by them.

You are in The Stormwright's Shelf, a neutral ledge in Sholazar Basin. The Shrine of the Tempest stands on its western side, where Rejek sends those carrying essences of wind and water to draw on the tempest's power. Its spirit healer offers a return to life, though not always yet. Storm Revenants and Aqueous Spirits roam the shelf, along with Stormwatchers and Perch Guardians.
You are in Death's Hand Encampment, a place in Sholazar Basin. Cultist Infiltrators prowl here.
